User-Friendly Intelligence Conclusion

How this evidence fits the mission

What the evidence shows

Nassar used medical and sporting authority to abuse patients and athletes over many years while institutions failed to stop him promptly.

Investigative lanes

child safeguardingmedical authoritysports governancelaw-enforcement failure

Why it matters

The case shows how professional expertise and institutional prestige can create repeated private access and suppress doubt.

Mechanism

Medical trust, treatment privacy, elite-sport hierarchy, fragmented complaints and delayed law-enforcement action.

Effect on the lane

Strongly strengthens authority-access and institutional-failure lanes.

What it points toward

Points toward mandatory cross-institution reporting, independent chaperoning and accountability for delayed referrals.

Strongest alternative explanation

Not every delay was intentional concealment; some reflected poor procedures, disbelief or jurisdictional confusion.

What it does not prove

It does not prove every coach, administrator, physician or agent knew of the abuse.

Evidence position

E6 convictions plus E5 inspector-general findings · Confidence: very high

Next investigative questions

  1. Which complaints reached which officials?
  2. What access controls failed?
  3. Which later victims could have been protected?

Classification rules, corrections and right of reply
  • A conviction label requires an adjudicated criminal outcome from an authoritative source.
  • Charges, indictments, complaints, arrests and investigations are not proof of guilt.
  • Civil, regulatory and canonical findings must not be described as state criminal convictions.
  • Dismissals, acquittals, reversals, withdrawals, pardons, denials and right-of-reply statements must remain attached to the claim.
  • Association or proximity is neutral unless reliable evidence establishes knowledge, facilitation, concealment, participation, obstruction or another relevant act.
  • Anonymous or unsourced allegations must not be published.
  • Every record requires provenance, date, legal status, evidence grade, counter-evidence, proof needed and a boundary statement.
  • Every existing criminal or safeguarding dossier represented in this registry must be regenerated and audited on every mission build.

Corrections, updated dispositions and documented responses must be added to the same subject record rather than silently replacing earlier history. Registry checked 2026-07-30.
